quizzes.stem: A team tags 50,000 short support tickets overnight, each with one of eight categories. Speed per ticket is irrelevant, spend matters, and the categories are easy to tell apart. What is the best first step?

options.a: Begin with the top tier, then step down if the budget complains
options.b: Begin with Claude Opus 5.5, because the overview names it the usual starting point
options.c: Begin with the lowest-priced tier and score it on genuine samples
options.d: Send the first thousand to each tier and keep whichever answers quickest

explanation.c: Simple, high-volume, cost-sensitive work fits the efficiency-first path, validated on real data (the two strategies).
explanation.a: Ruled out because the capability-first path is "Suited to complex reasoning, accuracy that outweighs cost, and high-autonomy agent work", and this task is the opposite.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the efficiency-first path says to "Begin with the fast, low-cost tier, test thoroughly, and move up only for a gap you can name", and the overview's default is only a starting point for most workloads.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the decision rule is to "compare accuracy, quality and edge-case handling", and speed per ticket is irrelevant here.

quizzes.stem: A coding agent running on the mid tier fails a handful of hard tasks each day. The team plans to move the entire system to the top tier. Which alternative should they try first?

options.a: Move all traffic to Claude Fable 5.1, then work the effort down later
options.b: Run the difficult cases at higher effort and measure the change
options.c: Drop to the fastest tier and retry each failure several times
options.d: Pin the id to a dated snapshot so results stop varying

explanation.b: The page says tuning effort is often a better lever than switching models, and a narrower change targets the hard tasks only.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the largest model "raises cost and latency on work that does not need it", and effort would do.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the efficiency-first path says to "move up only for a gap you can name", and retrying hard tasks on a weaker tier moves the wrong way.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "an id with a retirement date needs a migration plan before the date, not after" is about the life of an id and says nothing about capability.

quizzes.stem: A marketing manager with no engineering support needs weekly newsletters drafted in the house voice, using last quarter's issues as reference. Which approach fits best?

options.a: A Project in the app holding the tone guide and earlier editions
options.b: A scheduled script that calls the Messages API weekly with the issues attached
options.c: A bespoke agent on the Agent SDK that reads the archive before each draft
options.d: A cloud-platform deployment so the drafts stay inside the company account

explanation.a: A Project holds instructions and reference files for recurring non-developer work (the apps bullet and the first trap).
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A recurring chat workflow for a non-developer does not need code".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the Agent SDK row is for "Developers building custom agents", and a Project already holds the archive without code.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the cloud platforms row is for "Organisations that buy Claude through a cloud account", which the scenario never mentions.

quizzes.stem: A bank requires every call to a Claude model to run under the identity and permission rules of the hyperscaler it already buys infrastructure from. Developers still want the same models. Which option fits?

options.a: Give each developer a managed-agent environment under the bank's own tenancy
options.b: Keep calling the Messages API directly and add the bank's rules to the system prompt
options.c: Run Claude Code on every laptop, since it connects to the same engine everywhere
options.d: Take them through the matching cloud platform listing

explanation.d: The cloud platforms row carries the customer's cloud identity and permission model while serving the same models.
explanation.a: Ruled out because a managed agent suits "Teams with long-running, asynchronous work", and the page says nothing of it adopting the bank's tenancy.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "a cloud platform adds its own identity and permission model", while a system prompt only instructs the model.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the shared engine only means "your repo's CLAUDE.md files, settings, and MCP servers work across all of them", not that identity rules are enforced.

quizzes.stem: A developer wrote "answer in French" into a Project's instructions. Her own integration, calling the Messages API, still replies in English. What is the best explanation?

options.a: The Messages API supports fewer languages than the apps do
options.b: Settings kept in the chat product are not sent with requests from code
options.c: French must be requested through a model parameter that the API leaves unset
options.d: The integration needs the Agent SDK before it can follow language rules

explanation.b: Where instructions live decides where they are read, and a Project's instructions do not reach the API (the carry-across section and the third trap).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "The model is the same family behind every door, so its capabilities and its quirks are the same".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the instruction lives "In the API, in the system prompt your code sends", and no model parameter is involved.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Instructions written for one place do not appear in another unless you put them there", and no other surface is a precondition.

quizzes.stem: A team's research job runs for hours with nobody watching: mostly routine page fetching and note-taking, with a few hard judgment calls. Which design fits?

options.a: Host it in managed infrastructure, with cheap workers for bulk and a stronger model to decide
options.b: Chat through an app Project, with a person starting each step by hand
options.c: Run the strongest tier through the Messages API from the team's own servers
options.d: Use the fastest tier for every step, and add a stronger one only if the job fails

explanation.a: A job that runs for hours belongs in managed agents, and an orchestrator that hands bulk work to cheaper workers puts most tokens on the cheaper model while a stronger one takes the hard calls.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the apps give "Chat, Projects, artifacts, research, connectors; a person in the loop", and nobody is watching here.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the situation table points "A job runs for hours and should not tie up your servers" to managed agents.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "the cheapest model for everything under-serves exactly the cases that need depth".

quizzes.stem: A feature must call one specific Claude model for two years. In review, someone flags the id hard-coded in the source. What is the most likely concern?

options.a: Hard-coded ids bypass the pinned snapshot, so replies drift between calls
options.b: Dated ids are rejected by the Messages API in favour of aliases
options.c: A shorter alias would always follow new releases and should replace it
options.d: That snapshot has a retirement date, and nothing plans the move

explanation.d: The table shows retirement dates, and an id with a retirement date needs a migration plan before the date (the third trap).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "every Claude model id is a pinned snapshot", so replies do not drift under a fixed id.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "For Haiku 4.5 the dated id is the snapshot and the shorter name is an alias", so dated ids are accepted.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the page counts "including the dateless IDs used from the 4.6 generation on" among the pinned snapshots, so an alias is no more of a tracker.

quizzes.stem: A solo developer wants help restructuring a repository from the terminal, reading files and running the tests. Which surface fits best?

options.a: Claude Code, the agentic tool built for codebase work
options.b: The Agent SDK, to assemble a custom agent first
options.c: A Project in the app, with the files uploaded to its knowledge base
options.d: A Managed Agents session, since restructuring takes a while

explanation.a: Claude Code is the agentic coding tool that reads a codebase and runs commands.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the Agent SDK row is for "Developers building custom agents", and this developer wants help with a repository, not a new agent to build.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the Project row says "Instructions and uploads, not code", and a knowledge base cannot run the tests.
explanation.d: Ruled out because managed agents suit "Teams with long-running, asynchronous work", not an interactive refactor.

quizzes.stem: A team calls the same Claude model through the Claude API and through Amazon Bedrock, reusing one config file with a single name string for both. Both platforms list the model as current and access is granted, but Bedrock answers that the name is unknown. What is the most likely cause?

options.a: Bedrock runs a different generation of the family, so the name never matched
options.b: Each vendor gives the family its own id, so the value must differ
options.c: The account lacks the identity and permission setup that Bedrock requires
options.d: Bedrock already retired that model, so its name is unknown there

explanation.b: The cloud platforms bullet lists a separate id for each platform, for example anthropic.claude-opus-5-5 on Amazon Bedrock.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page says "Same model family; different ids, access and sometimes features", so the generation is the same and only the id differs.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the scenario grants access and the error concerns the name: "The ids differ, and the platform sets its own dates".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the scenario says both platforms list the model as current, as the page's example "anthropic.claude-opus-5-5 on Amazon Bedrock" shows for a current model.
